registered: 2026-11-15, after the Phase 6 development results and BEFORE any sealed-data result exists

hypothesis.title: Trend continuation outside contracting volatility
hypothesis.hypothesis: H1-trend continuation with an M15 break of structure produces positive expectancy when M15 volatility is not contracting.
hypothesis.origin: Development-derived, disclosed: generated on 15 November 2026 from the Phase 6 development results on January-13 November 2026, after five configurations and their breakdowns had been seen. The VOL-C baseline made +0.102 R/trade over 294 trades (9 of 11 months positive); its contracting-volatility trades made -0.171 R/trade over 31 trades. These development figures are the reason for the hypothesis and are NOT evidence for it. H6.4 is a new hypothesis, not a correction of H6.1, which stays recorded as not supported as predicted.
hypothesis.mechanism: Contracting M15 volatility marks compressed, range-bound conditions in which a break of structure has less follow-through; outside those conditions an H1-aligned M15 break tends to continue.
hypothesis.entry: Exactly VOL-C (H1 structure in the trade direction, a fresh M15 BOS in that direction within 2 candles, spread at most 0.50) plus one condition: M15 volatility normal or expanding (not contracting).
hypothesis.exit: Exactly VOL-C: stop beyond the unbroken M15 swing (0.1 ATR buffer), target 2R, at most 240 minutes.
hypothesis.not_included: No London-session filter or any other development-derived observation; one variable only.

config.name: Phase 6 H6.4: trend continuation outside contracting M15 volatility
config.description: H6.4 candidate: the VOL-C baseline with exactly one change (no entries while M15 volatility is contracting). Research only.

control.role: comparison baseline only: reported side by side, never selected instead of the candidate

prediction.text: On the sealed data: (1) the candidate's pooled M5 expectancy after costs is above zero; (2) the control's trades taken in contracting M15 volatility have a lower expectancy than its trades taken outside contracting volatility.

data.development: January-13 November 2026 (the Phase 6 development windows). One development run of candidate and control is made for debugging; its result is disclosed and does NOT decide whether the sealed test runs.
data.sealed_scored: November 2023 to October 2025: 24 calendar months, each a separate hypothetical $1,000 account; earlier candles (from mid-October 2023) are indicator warm-up only

coverage_rule.rule: A month is sufficient when present bars / expected bars >= 0.95 and the five-day warm-up exists. Expected bars come from the trading schedule; a MISSING bar inside a listed market-holiday closure window is removed from the expected count (a present bar always counts). Full closure on date D: window [D-1 22:00, D+1 00:00) UTC. Early close on date D: window [D 17:00, D+1 00:00) UTC. The list is fixed here, before any sealed result, and applies to every sealed month alike.
coverage_rule.resolution_december_2024: December 2024 measured 94.4 % (M15) and 94.5 % (H1) against the plain schedule. Every missing bar falls in the Christmas Eve early close (from 18:45 UTC on 24 Dec), Christmas Day (through the 26 Dec reopen hour) and the New Year's Eve early close; there are no other gaps. The threshold is kept; the expected count follows the market calendar.

costs: the frozen Phase 5 cost model: candle spread else $0.30, $3.50 per lot per side, $0.05 adverse slippage; 0.02 lots; next-open fills; stop-first
criteria: data: at least 18 of the 24 months have sufficient data (95 % coverage and warm-up); other months are INCOMPLETE and excluded
expectancy: pooled expectancy after costs > 0 R per trade
trade_count: at least 100 pooled trades (a minimum screen, not proof)
profit_factor: pooled profit factor at least 1.1
consistency: positive in at least 60 % of valid months, positive in each 12-month half (Nov 2023-Oct 2024 and Nov 2024-Oct 2025), and positive without its best month
prediction: the hypothesis's own prediction (regime, context or session difference) also holds on the sealed data
execution: still positive with spread and slippage doubled (tripled is reported only)
timeframes: run on M5 and on M15 execution; M15 positive as well
classes: promising (every criterion passes), inconclusive (positive but at least one criterion fails), rejected (pooled expectancy <= 0). Classes describe historical research candidates, not trading readiness.
one_shot: The sealed test runs once. A run that fails technically before producing any result may be restarted; every attempt is listed in the report. H6.4 is never retuned on its sealed result; a new idea needs a different hypothesis and unused data.
after: promising: further research (read-only paper-monitor observation on forward data at most; Phase 4 unchanged). inconclusive: recorded. rejected: recorded.
